sections.h2: Where is Eagan and what are its boundaries?
sections.html:
Eagan is a Dakota County city south of Saint Paul, on the south bank of the Minnesota River just upstream from where it meets the Mississippi. It has 31.18 square miles of land and about 945 feet of elevation, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 67,109 residents.

The northern edge follows Interstate 494, the eastern edge runs mostly along Minnesota Highway 3, the western edge is the river, and the southern boundary lies about a mile south of Cliff Road. Interstate 35E and Minnesota Highways 13, 55, 77 and 149 are the main routes. The ZIP codes are 55121, 55122 and 55123. The sparsely populated northern part of the city is convenient to the freeways and the Minneapolis-Saint Paul airport, which is why warehouses and distribution centers cluster there.

sections.h2: How did Eagan grow from farmland into a city of 67,000?
sections.html:
The city is named for Patrick Eagan, the first chairman of the town board, who farmed 220 acres near the present town hall. It was settled as an Irish farming community and was once called the onion capital of the United States. The town was established in 1860, and the city incorporated in 1972.

The big jump came in the 1980s, after Highway 77 was relocated and a six-lane bridge was built over the Minnesota River in 1980, followed by the last stretch of Interstate 35E in the mid-1980s.

  • 565 residents in 1860.
  • 3,382 in 1960 and 10,398 in 1970.
  • 20,700 in 1980 and 47,409 in 1990.
  • 63,557 in 2000 and 68,855 in 2020.
  • 67,109 in the 2025 estimate, about 2.5 percent below the 2020 estimate base.

The count more than doubled between 1980 and 1990, so many Eagan houses are now several decades old, and the original roofs, windows and kitchens of that growth period are common in resale listings.

sections.h2: Which employers and schools matter to Eagan buyers?
sections.html:
Eagan has a large corporate and logistics base. The city's 2025 financial report ranked its largest employers.

  • Thomson Reuters, with 4,500 employees.
  • Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Minnesota, with 3,000.
  • The U.S. Postal Service and Prime Therapeutics, each with about 2,100.
  • UPS with 1,500, Ecolab with 1,400 and the Rosemount-Apple Valley-Eagan school district with 1,075.

The Minnesota Vikings moved their headquarters and practice facility to the former Northwest Airlines site, and the Twin Cities Orthopedics Performance Center opened in 2018. The Census Bureau recorded $1.29 billion in transportation and warehousing receipts in Eagan for 2022.

Schools come from three districts: Rosemount-Apple Valley-Eagan (District 196), West St. Paul-Mendota Heights-Eagan (District 197) and Burnsville-Eagan-Savage (District 191). Eagan High School, Blackhawk Middle School and Dakota Hills Middle School belong to District 196. Check which district serves a specific address before you describe a school assignment in a listing.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about housing in Eagan?
sections.html:
The typical owner-occupied home in Eagan is valued near $397,000, and about a third of households rent. The table gives the main figures.

Households average 2.39 people, and 86.7 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so turnover is modest and a house that comes up for sale stands out.

sections.h2: Does an Eagan rental license pass to the buyer?
sections.html:
No. Eagan adopted its rental licensing ordinance on March 21, 2023, and licenses are issued each year and are not transferable, so a new owner must apply for a new license.

  • The 2026/27 fee is $165 per year for a single-unit rental, plus a $25 application fee and a $300 conversion fee when an owner-occupied home becomes a rental.
  • Every rental unit is inspected about once every three years or on complaint, and landlords give tenants at least 24 hours of notice.
  • Exempt rentals include units rented to the owner's qualifying relatives, state-licensed housing, rooms inside an owner-occupied home and contract-for-deed purchases recorded with Dakota County.

Late renewal costs 10 percent of the base fee in the first 30 days, 50 percent from 30 to 60 days and 100 percent after 60. Call Community Development at 651-675-5681 before you sell a tenant-occupied house. A buyer who plans to keep tenants has to apply for a license in their own name.

sections.h2: Which Eagan permits and property checks come up before a sale?
sections.html:
Eagan splits permits into two tracks. Building permits go through the online ePermits system, and Building Inspections at 651-675-5675 books inspections in 30-minute slots from 7:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. on weekdays. Zoning permits cover projects that need no building permit, and they are free.

Fences, patios, sport courts, driveway replacements, sidewalks, detached decks below 30 inches, one-story sheds up to 200 square feet, retaining walls under four feet and docks all fall under zoning permits. City staff generally answer within two to five business days. The city's property information page lets you view property records and check for special assessments, and most records include scanned permits, inspection history and site surveys that help a buyer see what was done.

On flood risk, the city says every property is in FEMA Flood Zone X except those in Zone AE along the Minnesota River. The maps date from December 2, 2011, so call the Planning Department or FEMA to confirm an address.

sections.h2: How does Dakota County record an Eagan deed?
sections.html:
Dakota County takes recorded documents only at the Administration Center in Hastings, either in person by appointment or by mail to Dakota County Property Taxation and Records, 1590 Highway 55, Hastings, MN 55033. Include a cover letter, a self-addressed stamped envelope and a phone number.

State deed tax is 0.33 percent of net consideration under Minnesota Statutes 287.21, so a sale at Eagan's $397,100 median value would carry about $1,310. Every transfer deed needs either a well disclosure certificate with a $54 fee or a well statement on the deed. Dakota County also says most of its property is abstract property, so a title company searches the records before closing. The Property Information Search shows tax statements and valuation notices for a parcel, and Property Taxation and Records answers questions at 651-438-4597.

Minnesota Statutes 513.55 requires you to give the buyer a written disclosure of known material facts before you sign.

sections.h2: When are Dakota County property taxes due for an Eagan house?
sections.html:
Real property tax is due in two halves, May 15 and October 15. The 2026 second half has passed, and the next deadline is May 15, 2027.

You can pay online through Paymentus with a 2.29 percent card fee, a $2.95 Visa debit fee or a $0.35 bank transfer fee, or by phone at 1-844-797-9075. In person, payments are accepted at the Hastings, West St. Paul and Apple Valley buildings, with weekday hours that end at 4:30 p.m. Mail must be postmarked on or before the due date. A free automatic payment program is open to owners whose taxes are not paid through a mortgage company.

A buyer who will live in the house should know that Dakota County lists December 31, 2026 as the homestead application deadline. Ask the title company how the year's taxes are prorated at closing.

sections.h2: What are your choices for selling a house in Eagan?
sections.html:
The three usual routes are a listing, a sale by owner and a direct cash purchase. Which one fits depends on the house, the timeline and whether tenants live there.

A listing aims at a family buyer and the highest price, and it fits a house in decent condition with time to show. A cash sale fits a rental owner facing a new license cycle, an owner relocating on a short timeline, or a house that needs updates from the 1980s and 1990s. Before you decide, ask each buyer for a written price and closing date, gather your permit history and any special assessment record, and compare the net amount rather than the headline number.

faqs.q: Does my Eagan rental license transfer to the person who buys my house?
faqs.a: No. Eagan issues licenses annually, they are not transferable, and a new owner must apply for a new rental license. Call Community Development at 651-675-5681 with questions.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Dakota County?
faqs.a: Deeds are recorded at the Property Taxation and Records office in the Administration Center in Hastings, by appointment, or by mail to 1590 Highway 55, Hastings, MN 55033. Include a cover letter, a stamped return envelope and a phone number.

faqs.q: Is my Eagan house in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Almost certainly not. The city says all properties are in FEMA Flood Zone X except those in Zone AE along the Minnesota River. The maps date from 2011, so confirm an address with Planning or FEMA.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace a fence or driveway in Eagan before selling?
faqs.a: Yes, a zoning permit, which is free. Fences, driveway replacements, patios, sheds up to 200 square feet and retaining walls under four feet are covered. Staff usually reply in two to five business days, and the Zoning Hotline is 651-675-5685.

faqs.q: When is the next Dakota County property tax payment due?
faqs.a: The next first-half payment is due May 15, 2027, and the second half follows on October 15. The second half for 2026 was due October 15, 2026.
